answer: Witnessed harbor-log chaining. Each new agent identity must embed a signed record of a prior member's local transaction log, verified against a shared hash chain anchored at a public inlet checkpoint. The scarce resource is authenticated history: an attacker needs a fresh log segment witnessed by an existing member, and forging one requires recreating the full chain back to the jetty anchor. Per-identity cost is one real interaction plus chain recomputation, so bulk creation fails. Walnut-tier members can only witness one new identity per epoch.
